time_scope: Blake & Breen 1971; Blake 1979; Dixon 1980 data summarized by Smith
claim: Pitta-Pitta has a general prohibition on word-initial liquids across places of articulation, in addition to the broader Australian restriction on anterior apicals, while word-initial glides are permitted.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Blake & Breen (1971:29) report six elicited liquid-initial forms; four are language/dialect names, and the remaining two are lateral-initial. These exceptions are tracked separately rather than erased.
section: 5.1 Rimal onglides are not subject to *ONSET/X

time_scope: Blake & Breen 1971 elicitation summarized by Smith
claim: The word-initial liquid restriction is not exceptionless: Blake & Breen elicited six liquid-initial forms, four of them language or dialect names and two beginning with laterals.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: These six forms are the counterexamples; their semantic concentration in proper language/dialect names suggests lexical/marginal status for most of the set.
section: 5.1 Rimal onglides are not subject to *ONSET/X

claim: Two rhotic-initial clan names are cited despite Blake's generalization that liquid-initial words are not generally found in Pitta-Pitta.
normalized_environment: RHOTIC / WORD_INITIAL in CLAN_NAMES despite general *LIQUID# restriction
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The two clan names are explicit exceptions to the ordinary-word generalization and should not be used to recode the language as freely allowing initial liquids.

time_scope: Blake & Breen 1971 and Blake 1979 descriptions reconciled by Smith
claim: Sources agree that word-initial /a/ is always preceded by a consonant; an onsetless initial low-vowel syllable is therefore not tolerated.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The high vowels /i,u/ are a separate disputed case and must not be generalized from this record.

claim: The surface status of homorganic glide plus high-vowel sequences word-initially is disputed: Blake & Breen report [ji]~[i] and [wu]~[u] variation, whereas Blake 1979 states that [yi] and [wu] are not heard initially and phonemicizes initial /i,u/ without the glides.

later_description: initial a does not occur onsetlessly

normalized_environment: WORD_INITIAL HOMORGANIC_GLIDE optionally/controversially realized before HIGH_VOWEL
scope: word-initial high vowels and homorganic glides
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Smith explicitly treats the facts as uncertain and offers alternative phonemic/OCP interpretations; no categorical surface rule should be promoted without direct acoustic or corpus verification.

claim: Stress is fixed on the word-initial syllable.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The cited discussion states that there are no proclitics, so proclitic-induced displacement is not part of the described pattern.

claim: Pitta-Pitta is reported to have no monosyllabic words.

time_scope: lexical phonotactic dataset based on Blake 1990
claim: Among word-initial laminal consonants before /u/, pre-palatal laminals account for 29% and dental laminals for 71% in Pitta Pitta, illustrating a gradient positional preference inside a maintained place contrast.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: This is a frequency asymmetry, not a categorical ban; both pre-palatal and dental laminals occur in the environment.
